title: Oxygen therapy, HFNC and NIV
summary: Prescribe oxygen to a target range, use high-flow nasal oxygen early in hypoxaemic respiratory failure and track the ROX index, apply NIV correctly in hypercapnic COPD and cardiogenic pulmonary oedema, recognise NIV failure early, and treat acute severe asthma stepwise.

topics.title: Oxygen prescription and SpO2 targets
topics.summary: Prescribe oxygen like a drug: SpO2 94-98% for most acutely ill patients (92-96% is a reasonable ICU range), 88-92% if at risk of hypercapnia. Avoid both hypoxaemia and hyperoxia; choose the right device.

steps.title: Assess
steps.detail: SpO2, RR, work of breathing, mental state; ABG if SpO2 < 94% on air, at risk of hypercapnia, or critically ill.

steps.title: Critical illness
steps.detail: Shock, sepsis, cardiac arrest, major trauma, anaphylaxis: start reservoir mask 15 L/min, then titrate down once stable.

steps.title: Pick a target
steps.detail: 94-98% for most patients; 88-92% for COPD with previous hypercapnia, obesity hypoventilation, neuromuscular or chest wall disease, cystic fibrosis.

steps.title: Device by need
steps.detail: Nasal cannula 1-4 L/min (FiO2 ~24-40%); simple face mask 5-10 L/min; Venturi 24-60% (fixed FiO2, ideal in hypercapnic risk); reservoir mask 15 L/min (~60-80%); HFNC if more is needed.

steps.title: Recheck gas
steps.detail: Repeat ABG/VBG within 30-60 min in hypercapnic-risk patients after any change in FiO2.

steps.title: Ventilated patients
steps.detail: Avoid hyperoxia (SpO2 persistently 100%, PaO2 > 100-150 mmHg). A PaO2 target of ~60 mmHg was not better than ~90 mmHg (HOT-ICU); many ICUs target SpO2 92-96%.

redFlags.text: Rising PaCO2 with falling pH on oxygen in COPD: reduce to target 88-92% and consider NIV.
SpO2 < 90% on reservoir mask: escalate to HFNC/NIV or intubation now.

pitfalls.text: Running a COPD patient at SpO2 98-100% on high-flow mask (worsens hypercapnia).
Pulse oximeters overestimate SpO2 in darker skin pigmentation and poor perfusion; confirm with ABG.
Carbon monoxide poisoning gives normal SpO2: use co-oximetry.

pearls.text: S/F ratio (SpO2/FiO2) can substitute for P/F when SpO2 ≤ 97%; S/F 315 ≈ P/F 300.
Cylinder duration (min) ≈ (cylinder pressure × cylinder factor) ÷ flow; use the calculator before transfers.

Maintain lowest FiO2 that meets target; wean

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Hypoxaemia mechanisms: low inspired O2, hypoventilation, V/Q mismatch, shunt, and diffusion limitation. Shunt responds poorly to FiO2 and needs PEEP or recruitment. In COPD, excess oxygen raises PaCO2 mainly through worsened V/Q matching (loss of hypoxic vasoconstriction) and the Haldane effect, not only by reduced drive.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- **BTS 2017:** 94-98% for most acutely ill adults; 88-92% for hypercapnic risk; prescribe a target range; reservoir mask for critical illness.
- **HOT-ICU (2021):** in 2928 ICU patients with acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure, PaO2 target 60 vs 90 mmHg gave similar 90-day mortality.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Exact optimum targets in ventilated patients (conservative vs liberal trials show mixed results).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Many Indian wards rely on cylinder oxygen and simple masks; Venturi masks are cheap and should be stocked for COPD.
- The COVID-19 oxygen crisis of 2021 showed the need for oxygen audits: avoid wasted flow when SpO2 is above target.

topics.title: High-flow nasal oxygen and the ROX index
topics.summary: HFNC is the first-line non-invasive support for acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure. Start at 50-60 L/min, titrate FiO2 to target, and use the ROX index at 2, 6 and 12 h to avoid delayed intubation.

steps.title: Acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure
steps.detail: SpO2 < 92% on ≥ 6-10 L/min, RR > 25-30, increased work of breathing, not hypercapnic. Also post-extubation in low-to-moderate risk patients and for preoxygenation.

steps.title: Settings
steps.detail: Flow 50-60 L/min (start 40 if not tolerated), FiO2 to SpO2 92-96%, temperature 37 °C (31-34 if uncomfortable). Largest prongs that fit (≤ 50% of nostril).

steps.title: ROX index
steps.detail: ROX = (SpO2/FiO2) ÷ RR. At 2, 6 and 12 h: ≥ 4.88 predicts success. < 2.85 at 2 h, < 3.47 at 6 h or < 3.85 at 12 h predicts failure.

steps.title: Do not delay intubation
steps.detail: Persisting high RR, thoraco-abdominal asynchrony, FiO2 > 0.7-0.8, falling ROX: intubate in a controlled way.

steps.title: When better
steps.detail: Reduce FiO2 first to ≤ 0.4, then flow in 5-10 L/min steps to 20-30 L/min, then switch to conventional oxygen.

tables.title: ROX index interpretation
tables.caption: Values in between are indeterminate: reassess in 1-2 h.

redFlags.text: FiO2 ≥ 0.8 at 60 L/min with SpO2 < 92%: intubation likely needed.
Patient exhausted, sweating, or confused despite HFNC.

pitfalls.text: Watching a 'reassuring' SpO2 while respiratory rate stays > 35/min.
Using HFNC in hypercapnic acidosis instead of NIV.

pearls.text: HFNC washes out dead space, generates ~1 cmH2O PEEP per 10 L/min with mouth closed, and is better tolerated than NIV.
A HACOR score (HR, acidosis, consciousness, oxygenation, RR) > 5 at 1 h predicts NIV failure in hypoxaemic patients.

nodes.text: ROX below failure threshold or worsening clinically?

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **FLORALI (2015):** HFNC vs standard oxygen vs NIV in non-hypercapnic AHRF: intubation rates did not differ significantly overall (38%, 47%, 50%) but were lower with HFNC in P/F ≤ 200; 90-day mortality was lower with HFNC.
- **ROX (2019):** validated thresholds at 2, 6 and 12 h.
- **ESICM 2023:** recommends HFNO over conventional oxygen to reduce intubation in AHRF (not due to COVID); no recommendation for or against NIV vs HFNO in non-COVID AHRF.
- **Hernández 2016:** HFNC was non-inferior to NIV for preventing reintubation in high-risk patients.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Helmet NIV vs HFNC in severe hypoxaemia; awake proning outside COVID-19.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - HFNC devices (including lower-cost Indian-made units) are now widespread but need a high-flow oxygen supply (up to 60 L/min); calculate cylinder or manifold capacity, especially in smaller hospitals.

topics.title: NIV in acute hypercapnic COPD exacerbation
topics.summary: Start NIV when pH < 7.35 and PaCO2 > 45 mmHg (6.5 kPa) persist after initial treatment. Titrate IPAP quickly, target SpO2 88-92%, recheck the gas at 1-2 h, and decide early whether NIV is working.

steps.title: Optimise medical treatment
steps.detail: Controlled O2 to 88-92%, nebulised salbutamol 5 mg + ipratropium 500 mcg (air-driven), prednisolone 40 mg, antibiotics if purulent sputum or ventilated.

steps.title: Decide on NIV
steps.detail: pH < 7.35 and PaCO2 > 45 mmHg (6.5 kPa) persisting despite optimal medical therapy. pH < 7.25: NIV in HDU/ICU with intubation ready.

steps.title: Settings
steps.detail: Full face (oronasal) mask. EPAP 4-5 cmH2O; IPAP 15 cmH2O, increasing to 20-30 cmH2O over 10-30 min as tolerated to reduce PaCO2. Backup rate 16-20. O2 entrained to SpO2 88-92%.

steps.title: ABG
steps.detail: Improving pH and RR = continue. No improvement: check mask leak, synchrony, settings, secretions; consider intubation.

steps.title: ABG again
steps.detail: Continue NIV as much as possible in the first 24 h, then wean during the day, keeping it overnight.

steps.title: Ceiling of treatment
steps.detail: Document whether intubation is appropriate before starting NIV.

tables.title: NIV settings for hypercapnic respiratory failure (BTS/ICS)
rows: Increase for upper airway obstruction (OSA, obesity) or to offset intrinsic PEEP

redFlags.text: pH < 7.25 or GCS falling: NIV only in ICU/HDU with immediate intubation available.
No improvement in pH or RR after 1-2 h of optimised NIV: consider intubation.
Contraindications: cardiac or respiratory arrest, inability to protect airway, copious secretions, facial trauma, undrained pneumothorax, vomiting, recent upper GI surgery.

pitfalls.text: Starting IPAP too low and never titrating (inadequate ventilation).
Large mask leak causing asynchrony and 'NIV failure'.

pearls.text: Obesity hypoventilation: higher EPAP (8-10+) is often needed to splint the upper airway.

nodes.text: pH < 7.35 and PaCO2 > 45 mmHg after 1 h treatment?
Continue medical therapy; repeat ABG if worsens
Intubate (if appropriate to ceiling of care)
ABG at 1-2 h: pH and RR improving?
Continue; recheck at 4-6 h; wean after 24-48 h

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Dynamic hyperinflation increases the work of breathing and intrinsic PEEP. NIV unloads the respiratory muscles (IPAP) and offsets intrinsic PEEP (EPAP), increasing alveolar ventilation and lowering PaCO2.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ERS/ATS 2017:** strong recommendation for bilevel NIV in COPD exacerbation with acute or acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis (pH ≤ 7.35).
- **BTS/ICS 2016:** start NIV when pH < 7.35 and PaCO2 > 6.5 kPa persist despite immediate medical therapy; specific titration advice.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Role of HFNC in mild hypercapnia (pH 7.25-7.35) if NIV is not tolerated: emerging data, not guideline-standard.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- COPD in India is often driven by biomass fuel exposure, especially in women; tuberculosis sequelae can coexist (post-TB obstructive disease).
- The joint ICS/NCCP (India) guideline supports NIV for acute hypercapnic exacerbations.

topics.title: NIV and CPAP beyond COPD
topics.summary: CPAP or bilevel NIV is strongly indicated for cardiogenic pulmonary oedema, useful in immunocompromised and post-operative respiratory failure, can prevent post-extubation failure in high-risk patients, but should not be used to rescue established post-extubation failure.

steps.title: CPAP or bilevel
steps.detail: CPAP 8-10 cmH2O (or bilevel) with FiO2 to target; plus nitrates if BP allows and diuretics. Strong recommendation.

steps.title: Early NIV or HFNC
steps.detail: Conditional recommendation for NIV in ERS/ATS; HFNC is often preferred now.

steps.title: Abdominal or thoracic surgery
steps.detail: NIV for post-operative acute respiratory failure (conditional).

steps.title: Prevention in high risk
steps.detail: Prophylactic NIV (alternating with HFNC) reduces reintubation in high-risk patients (HIGH-WEAN). Do NOT use NIV to rescue established post-extubation respiratory failure.

steps.title: Early NIV
steps.detail: Conditional recommendation in hypoxaemic chest trauma with adequate analgesia.

steps.title: Caution
steps.detail: No recommendation for NIV over HFNC (ESICM 2023); if used, avoid large tidal volumes (> 9.5 mL/kg PBW) and intubate promptly if failing.

steps.title: Dyspnoea relief
steps.detail: NIV may be offered for dyspnoea in palliative care if it improves comfort.

tables.title: ERS/ATS 2017 NIV recommendations
rows: Prevention of post-extubation ARF in high risk

redFlags.text: Expired tidal volume > 9.5 mL/kg PBW on NIV in hypoxaemic failure predicts failure (patient self-inflicted lung injury risk).

pitfalls.text: Continuing NIV for hours in pneumonia while the patient tires: delayed intubation.

pearls.text: Helmet NIV allows higher PEEP with less leak and is better tolerated for long periods.

nodes.text: Acute respiratory failure, no immediate intubation need
Hypercapnic COPD: bilevel NIV (see NIV in COPD)
Cardiogenic pulmonary oedema: CPAP 8-10 or bilevel + treat cause
Hypoxaemic (pneumonia, ARDS, immunocompromised): HFNC first; NIV/helmet in selected cases
After extubation, high risk: prophylactic HFNC ± NIV; established failure → reintubate

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ERS/ATS 2017:** see table.
- **HIGH-WEAN (2019):** HFNC + NIV after extubation reduced reintubation vs HFNC alone (11.8% vs 18.2%) in high-risk patients.
- **Hernández 2016:** HFNC was non-inferior to NIV after extubation in high-risk patients.
consultantNotes.controversies: - NIV vs HFNC in immunocompromised patients: recent trials favour HFNC or show no difference.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Many Indian wards use ICU ventilators in NIV mode with a full face mask; check for leak compensation and set alarms appropriately.

topics.title: Acute severe and life-threatening asthma
topics.summary: Grade severity quickly (PEF, speech, RR, HR, SpO2, PaCO2). Give oxygen-driven salbutamol, ipratropium and steroids at once; add IV magnesium; a normal or rising PaCO2 is a danger sign; intubate early and ventilate to avoid breath stacking.

steps.title: Grade severity
steps.detail: Acute severe: PEF 33-50% predicted/best, RR ≥ 25, HR ≥ 110, cannot complete sentences. Life-threatening: PEF < 33%, SpO2 < 92%, PaO2 < 60 mmHg (8 kPa), normal PaCO2 (35-45 mmHg), silent chest, cyanosis, poor effort, arrhythmia, exhaustion, altered consciousness, hypotension. Near-fatal: raised PaCO2.

steps.title: Oxygen
steps.detail: Target SpO2 93-95%.

steps.title: Bronchodilators
steps.detail: Salbutamol 5 mg nebulised with oxygen, repeated every 15-30 min (or continuous 5-10 mg/h); add ipratropium 500 mcg every 4-6 h in severe/life-threatening attacks.

steps.title: Steroids
steps.detail: Prednisolone 40-50 mg orally (or hydrocortisone 100 mg IV every 6 h); continue ≥ 5 days.

steps.title: IV magnesium
steps.detail: 1.2-2 g IV over 20 min, single dose.

steps.title: Senior / ICU
steps.detail: Consider IV aminophylline (senior decision), IV salbutamol only if inhaled therapy cannot be used; ketamine infusion as bridge; ABG for rising PaCO2.

steps.title: When
steps.detail: Exhaustion, falling GCS, rising PaCO2 with acidosis, arrest. Use ketamine induction, large tube (≥ 8.0), most experienced operator.

steps.title: Avoid breath stacking
steps.detail: Low rate 8-12, Vt 6-8 mL/kg PBW, short Ti, high inspiratory flow, I:E ≥ 1:4, accept PaCO2 rise (permissive hypercapnia, pH > 7.2), plateau < 30, measure intrinsic PEEP. If hypotension: disconnect and compress the chest gently.

Silent chest, cyanosis, confusion, bradycardia, hypotension.
Hypotension after intubation: dynamic hyperinflation or tension pneumothorax.

pitfalls.text: Sedating an agitated hypoxic asthmatic on the ward.
Treating with high respiratory rate on the ventilator (breath stacking, barotrauma, cardiac arrest).

pearls.text: Measure intrinsic PEEP with an end-expiratory hold; plateau pressure < 30 cmH2O and auto-PEEP < 10 cmH2O are reasonable targets.

O2 to 93-95%, salbutamol 5 mg + ipratropium 500 mcg nebulised, steroids

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **BTS/SIGN 2019 (amended 2024):** severity criteria, oxygen-driven nebulised beta-2 agonist, ipratropium in severe attacks, steroids, IV magnesium single dose; aminophylline only after senior consultation.
- **GINA:** similar acute management; SpO2 93-95% target.
consultantNotes.controversies:
- Ketamine infusion and inhalational anaesthetics as rescue: case series only.
- NIV in asthma: limited evidence; only in ICU with close monitoring.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Ipratropium-salbutamol combination respules are widely used in India; dose by the salbutamol component.
- Aminophylline and deriphylline (etofylline + theophylline) are frequently used in Indian emergency departments; guidelines support them only after senior review because of toxicity.

drugs.name: Salbutamol (albuterol)
drugs.indications: Acute asthma and COPD exacerbation; hyperkalaemia (adjunct).
drugs.adultDose: Nebulised 5 mg (oxygen-driven in asthma, air-driven in hypercapnic COPD) repeated every 15-30 min, or continuous 5-10 mg/h in severe asthma. MDI with spacer 4-10 puffs (100 mcg/puff) every 20 min is equivalent in less severe attacks. IV 5 mcg/min up to 20 mcg/min only if inhaled route is not possible (senior decision).
drugs.preparationIndia: Respules 2.5 mg/2.5 mL and 5 mg/2.5 mL; nebuliser solution 5 mg/mL; MDI 100 mcg/puff.
drugs.cautions: Tachycardia, hypokalaemia, lactic acidosis (type B), tremor.
drugs.monitoring: Potassium and lactate when giving repeated or continuous doses.

drugs.name: Ipratropium bromide
drugs.indications: Acute severe or life-threatening asthma; COPD exacerbation.
drugs.adultDose: 500 mcg nebulised every 4-6 h (may be given every 20 min for the first hour in severe asthma).
drugs.preparationIndia: Respules 500 mcg/2 mL; often combined with salbutamol (Duolin-type respules: levosalbutamol or salbutamol + ipratropium).

drugs.name: Magnesium sulfate
drugs.indications: Acute severe or life-threatening asthma not responding to initial inhaled therapy.
drugs.adultDose: 1.2-2 g IV over 20 min, single dose.
drugs.preparationIndia: 50% w/v (500 mg/mL) 2 mL ampoules: 2 g = 4 mL, diluted in 100 mL NS.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension, flushing; caution in renal failure (repeated doses).

drugs.name: Prednisolone / hydrocortisone
drugs.indications: All acute asthma attacks; COPD exacerbation.
drugs.adultDose: Asthma: prednisolone 40-50 mg orally daily for at least 5 days, or hydrocortisone 100 mg IV every 6 h if unable to swallow. COPD: prednisolone 40 mg daily for 5 days.
drugs.preparationIndia: Prednisolone 5, 10, 20, 40 mg tablets; hydrocortisone 100 mg vials. Methylprednisolone 40 mg IV is a common Indian ICU alternative.
drugs.cautions: Hyperglycaemia; myopathy with high doses and neuromuscular blockers.

drugs.name: Aminophylline
drugs.indications: Life-threatening asthma not responding to inhaled therapy (senior decision only).
drugs.adultDose: Load 5 mg/kg IV over 20 min (omit if on oral theophylline), then 0.5 mg/kg/h; check levels (10-20 mg/L).
drugs.cautions: Narrow therapeutic index: arrhythmias, seizures, vomiting; interactions (ciprofloxacin, clarithromycin, erythromycin raise levels).
